newsitem.title: CANADA: Barrick sees higher production, cash flow.
newsitem.headline: Barrick sees higher production, cash flow.

text.p: Barrick Gold Corp said on Monday it expected production to rise in the second half of 1997, generating a corresponding improvement in the gold miner's financial performance.
"Production will be substantially higher in the second half, allowing us to achieve our production target for the year of over three million ounces," Barrick President John Carrington said.
"With this level of production, we expect 1997 earnings to be comparable to 1996 and cash flow to rise to about a half-billion dollars," he added.

Barrick said its Goldstrike property would post significantly increased production in the second half, due mainly to mine sequencing in the Betze-Post Pit, which will access higher grade ounces later in the year.
Cash operating costs were expected to be on target at US$190 per ounce for 1997, as production increased in the second half of the lower cost Betze-Post Mine, Barrick said.

Barrick's first-quarter earnings declined to US$0.15 a share from US$0.20 a year earlier, while gold production was 712,368 ounces in the first quarter compared to 800,515 ounces in the same period a year earlier.
